signals.observe: Read the SKU (order code) on the sticker on the back of the unit or on the box.
signals.caveats: Stickers come off and boxes get thrown away. A suffix-less SKU (K001, K007, K010) covers several revisions. C145 (Tab5) and K145 (Tab5 Kit) each cover all three Tab5 revisions.

signals.observe: The colour of the power LED while the unit is on.
signals.caveats: Splits Core2 v1.1 (blue, AXP2101) from the AXP192 Core2 revisions only. Green does not tell v1.0 from v1.3.

signals.observe: The USB vendor ID of the serial port (Device Manager > Details > Hardware Ids on Windows, lsusb on Linux, System Information on macOS; doctor.py prints it).
signals.caveats: Core2 v1.0 and Core2 for AWS v1.0 shipped with either bridge, so CH9102 never proves a later revision of either. Only CP2104 rules revisions in. The bridge on Gray and on Fire before v2.7 is undocumented.

signals.observe: Run `esptool flash-id` (or `esptool.py flash_id`) on the port; read 'Detected flash size'. Read-only.
signals.caveats: Basic only: flash went from 4 MB to 16 MB in 2020.6.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that reads register 0x03 of the chip at I2C 0x34 on the internal bus.

AXP192.datasheet_gap: The value comes from M5Unified. The AXP192 datasheet (v1.13) does not document register 0x03. A hardware run on a Core2 v1.3 settles it.

AXP2101.datasheet_gap: The value comes from M5Unified. The one AXP2101 datasheet that documents register 0x03 (rev 0.1, 2019) gives 0x47 or 0x57, not 0x4A. A hardware run on a Core2 v1.1 or a CoreS3-family unit settles it.

signals.caveats: Needs flashing, and is inferred from a chip ID. The two PMICs share address 0x34, so an address scan alone cannot tell them apart.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that reads the IMU identity register: 0x75 at I2C 0x68 (MPU family), or 0x00 at 0x68/0x69 (BMI270).
signals.caveats: Needs flashing, and is inferred from a chip ID. Fire 2019.7 (SH200Q) is not covered. The MPU-9250 register map (RM-MPU-9250A-00 rev 1.4) contradicts itself on register 0x75: its header gives a reset value of 0x68, its text a default of 0x71. The data expects 0x71, as M5Unified does; a reading of 0x68 at 0x75 is ambiguous between an MPU-9250 and an MPU-6050.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that reads 16-bit register 0xFF of the chip at I2C 0x40 on the internal bus.
signals.caveats: Core2 family only. On CoreS3 an ES7210 audio codec sits at 0x40, so presence at that address means nothing there.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that wakes the ATECC608B, then reads 4 bytes from I2C 0x35 and compares them with the wake reply.

absent.value: no ACK at 0x35 after the wake

probe.note: Wake by holding SDA low for at least 60 us, or by sending 0x00 as the address byte at 100 kHz (nothing ACKs it), then wait at least 1500 us (SelfTest does not run at wake on the TNGTLS part). A plain read with no word address returns count 0x04, status 0x11 (after wake, before the first command) and a CRC-16. The chip ignores a wake while already awake, and 0x11 is only returned before its first command, so run the probe before anything else talks to it. The CRC bytes 0x33 0x43 are computed with the data sheet's rule (polynomial 0x8005, initial value 0), not quoted from it.

signals.caveats: Needs flashing. The ATECC608B sleeps; a plain address scan may miss it.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that scans the internal I2C bus for 0x38 and 0x2E.
Flash a sketch that scans the internal I2C bus for the IP5306 at 0x75.
signals.caveats: Gray only. M5 documents the late I2C wiring for Gray alone.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that prints the PSRAM size (ESP.getPsramSize() in Arduino).
signals.caveats: Fire only: PSRAM went from 4 MB to 8 MB in 2020.4.

signals.observe: On the pin map printed on the back of the Tab5, read the driver named in the '5" IPS-LCD' box.
signals.caveats: Tab5 only. M5's note about the label was written for the change to the ST7123; its picture shows an ST7123 unit, and M5 does not show the label of an ILI9881C or an ST7121 unit.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that scans the internal I2C bus for 0x14 and 0x55.
signals.caveats: Needs flashing. Tab5 only. It cannot tell the ST7123 from the ST7121: both answer at 0x55. A GT911 answers at 0x14 only when its interrupt line (G23) is high as it leaves reset, and at 0x5D otherwise; M5GFX drives G23 high and tries both.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that reads 16-bit register 0xFF of the chip at I2C 0x41 on the internal bus.
signals.caveats: Needs flashing. Tab5 only; it is on every Tab5 revision, so it confirms the part and splits nothing.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that reads register 0x01 of the I/O expander at I2C 0x43 on the internal bus.

probe.note: Register 0x01 holds the manufacturer ID (101) in bits 7 to 5, the firmware revision (000) in bits 4 to 2 and a reset flag in bit 1. The flag is set after any reset and clears when the register is read, so the first read after a reset gives 0xA2 and later ones 0xA0. M5GFX reads the register while it detects the board, so a probe that runs after M5.begin() reads 0xA0; one that runs before it reads 0xA2, which the smoke program prints as present raw 0xA2.

signals.caveats: Needs flashing. Tab5 only; it is on every Tab5 revision, so it confirms the part and splits nothing.

signals.observe: Flash a sketch that scans the internal I2C bus for 0x10 (ES8388), 0x32 (RX8130CE) and 0x40 (ES7210).

probe.note: Presence only: the ES8388 and ES7210 datasheets M5 links and the RX8130CE register manual name no identification register, so an answer at the address is all this reads (ADR 0005).

signals.caveats: Needs flashing. Tab5 only. An answer at an address does not name the chip, and all three are on every Tab5 revision, so it splits nothing.
